input_text: Albert is being sued by Tim for breach of contract. The issue is whether Albert knew at the time signing the contract that he had no intention of following through. Tim's lawyers introduce an email Albert wrote to his friend saying he wasn't planning on honoring the contract with Tim.

extraction.input_text: Albert is being sued by Tim for breach of contract. The issue is whether Albert knew at the time signing the contract that he had no intention of following through. Tim's lawyers introduce an email Albert wrote to his friend saying he wasn't planning on honoring the contract with Tim.

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The statement was made out of court, as it was an email written by Albert to his friend prior to the litigation.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c)(1) - Hearsay requires an out-of-court statement.
arguments.evidence_span: an email Albert wrote to his friend

arguments.text: The statement contains a clear assertion, as Albert explicitly stated he was not planning on honoring the contract.
arguments.evidence_span: saying he wasn't planning on honoring the contract with Tim

arguments.text: The statement is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted, specifically to establish Albert's knowledge and intent at the time of signing the contract.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c)(3) - Hearsay requires the statement to be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: The issue is whether Albert knew at the time signing the contract that he had no intention of following through.

arguments.text: The statement qualifies as an admission by a party-opponent under FRE 801(d)(2), as it is a statement made by Albert, the defendant, offered against him by Tim.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(d)(2)(A) - A statement offered against an opposing party and made by that party is not hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: Albert is being sued by Tim... Tim's lawyers introduce an email Albert wrote
